description: Four-panel composite of SEM fractographs of fracture surfaces, one per steel, each labelled in a white box at the top-left: (a) 3Cr, (b) 2Ni, (c) 2Ni3Cr, (d) 2Ni5Cr. Every main panel is a secondary-electron image of the fibre zone carrying a 200 µm scale bar at the bottom-right. All four surfaces show a fully dimpled microvoid-coalescence morphology: dense networks of rounded to elongated dimples separated by thin tear ridges, with a scatter of larger, deeper circular holes (probable particle/inclusion sites) and locally coarser, irregularly shaped voids. Dimple populations differ in apparent size and depth between panels — (c) 2Ni3Cr looks the finest and most uniform, (d) 2Ni5Cr the coarsest with deeper pits — but no dimple dimension is printed anywhere; only the 200 µm scale bar fixes scale. An inset at the top-right of each panel shows the macroscopic fracture surface: a dark, elongated rectangular specimen with a brighter central band (the fibrous zone) flanked by shear lips. Taken together the four panels argue that all four ultra-fast-cooled steels (3Cr, 2Ni, 2Ni3Cr, 2Ni5Cr) fail by ductile microvoid coalescence regardless of Ni/Cr balance, with no cleavage facets evident.

subfigures.description: SEM fractograph of the 3Cr steel fibre zone; dimpled microvoid-coalescence surface with fine tear ridges and several larger deep circular holes, plus a coarser elongated void region; 200 µm scale bar bottom-right; top-right inset shows the whole macroscopic fracture surface (dark elongated specimen with bright central band).

SEM fractograph of the 2Ni steel fibre zone; dimple network with larger, deeper rounded holes and rough tear ridges; 200 µm scale bar bottom-right; top-right inset of the macroscopic fracture surface.

SEM fractograph of the 2Ni3Cr steel fibre zone; appears the finest, most uniform and least deep dimple population of the four panels, but this ranking is visual only; 200 µm scale bar bottom-right; top-right inset of the macroscopic fracture surface.

SEM fractograph of the 2Ni5Cr steel fibre zone; coarser, more irregular dimples with pronounced deep pits and prominent tear ridges; 200 µm scale bar bottom-right; top-right inset of the macroscopic fracture surface.

observations.observation: The figure is a 2x2 group of SEM fracture-surface images labelled (a) 3Cr, (b) 2Ni, (c) 2Ni3Cr and (d) 2Ni5Cr, each label printed in a white box at the panel top-left.
Every main micrograph contains a scale bar annotated '200 µm' in the bottom-right corner.
All four panels show a dimpled microvoid-coalescence surface with ductile tear ridges and no flat cleavage facets; no quantitative dimple size is printed on any panel.
Each panel contains a few larger, deeper circular holes in addition to the fine dimples, which are localised and markedly larger than the surrounding dimple population.

An inset at the top-right of each panel shows a dark, elongated rectangular specimen with a bright central band, i.e. the whole macroscopic fracture surface rather than a magnified view; the insets carry no visible scale bar or labels.
The caption identifies the four panels as SEM images of the fracture surfaces of (a) 3Cr, (b) 2Ni, (c) 2Ni3Cr and (d) 2Ni5Cr steel.

The citing text states that the images show the fibre zone of the UFCed (ultra-fast-cooled) 3Cr, 2Ni, 2Ni3Cr and 2Ni5Cr steels and that the insets show the macroscopic morphology of the fracture surfaces.
The citing text states that a large number of dimples is observed in the fibre zone of all four steels and concludes that they all fracture in a ductile mode.

Dimple populations appear to differ between panels (finest/most uniform in (c) 2Ni3Cr, coarsest with deeper pits in (d) 2Ni5Cr), but this ranking is based on visual impression only and cannot be quantified from the image.
